overall: The AG found the Council, its License Committee and its Rules and Ordinance Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by deliberating via email, intentionally, and ordered compliance and release of the offending emails; two Spadafora emails were not deliberation.

allegations.summary: Councilor Sica's January 21 email to a quorum of the License Committee allegedly deliberated on a license matter outside a noticed meeting.
allegations.key_passage: we find that Councilor Sica violated the Open Meeting Law by deliberating outside of a properly noticed meeting via email.

allegations.summary: Councilor Spadafora's January 26 'Green Space Resolve' email to the full Council allegedly deliberated on public business outside a noticed meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, Councilor Spadafora’s January 26 email constituted deliberation outside of a properly noticed meeting.

allegations.summary: Councilor Spadafora's January 26 and 28 replies to the Mayor's Special Assistant, copied to the Council, allegedly deliberated outside a meeting.
allegations.key_passage: We find that Councilor Spadafora’s January 26 and 28 emails responding to the Special Assistant to the Mayor do not constitute deliberation because they do not relate to business within the Council’s jurisdiction.

allegations.summary: February 21-22 emails among a quorum of the Rules and Ordinance Committee on handling the Malden River zoning papers allegedly deliberated outside a noticed meeting.
allegations.key_passage: we ultimately find that these emails also constitute deliberation outside of a noticed meeting in violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainants alleged the email deliberations were intentional violations of the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: Because we have previously clearly warned the Council that deliberation via email violates the Open Meeting Law, we find the violations here to be intentional.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law by the Council and the Committees.
Within 30 days of the letter, release to the public the emails found to violate the Open Meeting Law.
remedy_passage: We order the Council and the Committees’ immediate and future compliance. Additionally, we order the Council and the Committees to, within 30 days of the date of this letter, release to the public the emails found here to be in violation of the Open Meeting Law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
